warning: These units are a research projection over the frozen owner-native sources. They do not replace product authority and are deliberately multi-axis after EX1 falsified a single-primary-owner explanation ontology.

ownershipAxes.semanticChoice: Who decides meaning, relevance, strategy, scientific/domain validity, or whether a candidate should be accepted?
ownershipAxes.durableStructuralState: Which subsystem persists and validates the structural identity/state needed for continuity?
ownershipAxes.physicalTruth: Which owner proves what physically executed, exists, changed, stopped, or produced exact bytes?
ownershipAxes.externalEffectTruth: Which external provider/domain/structured adapter can prove the externally visible effect itself?
ownershipAxes.sharingDisposition: Should the mechanism be shared across Ordivon, remain domain/local, delegate to mature substrate, or not exist yet?

crossAxisExamples.note: The Agent chooses which exact sources remain current cognition; Harness persists/proves pins and transitions without ranking relevance.

crossAxisExamples.durableStructuralState: Host may record verification and Task outcome admission
crossAxisExamples.physicalTruth: Runtime proves the executable result and Artifacts
crossAxisExamples.note: Physical success, semantic judgment and durable outcome admission are different facts.

crossAxisExamples.case: arbitrary shell command that may send an external payment/message/order
crossAxisExamples.physicalTruth: Runtime proves only the admitted local execution
crossAxisExamples.externalEffectTruth: external provider/domain receipt or reconciliation state
crossAxisExamples.sharingDisposition: domain/local unless a structured effect contract earns a narrower shared owner
crossAxisExamples.note: Runtime Execution Result != External Effect Receipt.

crossAxisExamples.sharingDisposition: delegate to classical substrate; therefore no new Ordivon shared mechanism is justified
crossAxisExamples.note: CLASSICAL_SUBSTRATE and NO_NEW_SHARED_LAYER are compatible dimensions, not competing primary-owner labels.

units.reality: Useful work, commitments and unresolved semantic state can outlive any one model/chat/Agent Run or physical process, and multiple replacement sessions may race to continue the same work.
units.pressure: If long-lived work identity is owned by a transient cognition or process, session loss erases the current frontier; if competing sessions have no exact semantic revision, both can claim incompatible continuation; irreversible/shared consequences also need durable commitment and participant decision identity before delivery.
classicalBaseline: SQLite can transactionally persist rows and compare revisions.
Git can preserve source history and exact revisions.
Issue trackers can record human-oriented work items.
None of those facts by themselves defines Ordivon's current Task semantics, consequence admission, verification record, or external-Agent recovery contract.
units.residualMissingResponsibility: One durable semantic work/commitment plane that preserves Task identity, exact revision, bounded semantic checkpoint/context, explicit consequence admission, verification and Task outcome while treating cognition and physical execution as replaceable dependencies.
units.counterfactualDeletion: Remove Host while keeping Harness, Runtime, Git and databases: bounded Runs and physical Jobs can still execute, but the system loses one revision-fenced semantic identity for what long-lived work still exists, what commitments/unknowns remain, which participant decision is pending, and which verified result may close that work. Each caller must rebuild this semantics or collapse work back into sessions.
units.semanticChoice: Participant/domain/Agent supplies purpose, proposals and domain judgments; Host admits only the semantic transitions it is authorized to own.
units.physicalTruth: Not Host. Re-read Runtime/Git/provider/domain owners through exact references.
units.externalEffectTruth: Not generic Host truth; provider/domain or a narrow workload effect contract supplies occurrence evidence.
proofBoundaries: WorkingCheckpoint is a semantic working claim, not copied Runtime/Git/domain truth.
Host does not own Provider invocation or Agent Run continuity.
Runtime success alone cannot complete a Host Task.
A Host terminal continuity disposition says whether Host should keep tracking the external work; it does not assert success in an external domain.
Host is not a universal scheduler or participant hierarchy.
evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md guarded-mutation response-loss path: persist Dispatch identity, classify UNKNOWN, locate original Runtime Job, verify independently, never blind redispatch
current six-tool Host MCP separation between observation/recovery and writes
units.disposition: retain; narrow responsibility boundary is well-supported
units.expectedCapability: A replacement Agent can resume the same semantic work after session/process replacement, revalidate external truth, coordinate competing continuations by exact revision, and preserve commitments/unknowns instead of making the chat transcript the work authority.
commonMisconceptions: Host checkpoint is a cached copy of reality.
Host Task outcome may override domain truth.
units.feynman: Host is the durable notebook and commitment ledger for unfinished work. It remembers what work still means and what has been accepted, but when you resume it tells you where to re-check the real machine and real domain rather than pretending its notes are reality.

units.reality: One bounded cognition episode has structural state that is neither the parent Task nor an operating-system process: selected current cognition, caller interaction, attempt-local Tool observations, exact Provider call state, Tool action surface, budgets, response-loss and pause/resume continuity.
units.pressure: A Provider SDK can issue model requests, but callers otherwise repeatedly reconstruct the same model-Tool loop, provider retry/UNKNOWN semantics, current-cognition selection, action fencing and Run recovery. Treating complete history as current cognition also anchors obsolete evidence and conflates storage with selection.
classicalBaseline: Host can preserve a long-lived Task.
None alone owns the bounded Agent Run's structural cognition + Provider/Tool continuity.
units.residualMissingResponsibility: A caller-neutral bounded Agent Run authority that preserves exact structural cognition/execution state while leaving semantic reasoning, relevance and strategy to the Agent and final acceptance to caller/domain authority.
candidateMechanism: request-bound execution control and exact Tool surface
units.counterfactualDeletion: Remove Harness while keeping Host, Runtime and Provider SDKs: long-lived Tasks and physical execution remain possible, but each application must rebuild exact Provider-call recovery, model-Tool sequencing, current-cognition selection/provenance, action-surface fencing, Run budgets and candidate completion evidence. Provider-specific continuation state tends to leak either upward into Task authority or disappear on recovery.
units.semanticChoice: Agent chooses semantic reasoning, action, Strategy and which exact available sources remain selected cognition; caller/domain verifies final meaning.
units.durableStructuralState: Harness owns the Run's exact structural cognition, Provider/Tool lifecycle and recovery evidence.
units.physicalTruth: Runtime or external Tool owner, not Harness.
units.externalEffectTruth: External provider/domain/structured Tool owner; Harness proves intent/fence/receipt linkage, not arbitrary world success.
proofBoundaries: History != Cognition; Storage != Selection; Observation != Retention.
Agent semantic choice != Harness structural truth.
Tool Intent != Physical Effect; Physical Effect != Semantic Success.
Harness candidate_completed / CompletionProposal != Task or domain completion.
Generic Memory/RAG/ranking/summarization is not a Harness default.

units.disposition: retain; keep cognition sovereignty and proof-boundary inequalities explicit
units.expectedCapability: An Agent can run against replaceable Providers/Tools with exact bounded cognition and recovery, choose its own current knowledge instead of receiving infrastructure-selected memory, and return a candidate result whose provenance can be independently judged by its caller.
commonMisconceptions: Harness should choose relevant Context for the Agent.
Harness Run completion means the Task is done.

units.feynman: Harness is the flight recorder and control rig for one stretch of thinking. It remembers exactly what the Agent was allowed to see and do, what the model/provider/tool exchange actually was, and how to resume it, but it does not decide what the evidence means or whether the larger job is truly finished.

units.reality: An Agent proposal is not physical reality. After admission, crash, timeout, cancellation, source/provider drift or response loss can make it unclear which exact operation ran, whether descendants remain, and which result bytes belong to that execution.
units.pressure: Linux/systemd/Git/SQLite/files each own strong local facts, but without one cross-bound operation identity an Agent caller still has to guess how a semantic request maps to Workspace/source state, one physical dispatch generation, one process tree, bounded evidence and recovery after interruption.
classicalBaseline: systemd/cgroups own process-tree supervision and resource enforcement.
digest-bound files own retained Result/Artifact bytes.
Runtime delegates to these owners rather than creating a second proof system.
units.residualMissingResponsibility: Convert one admitted Agent-generated local operation into stable world-bound physical identity, dispatch it at most once per Attempt, bind execution preconditions, retain exact evidence, and reconcile known/unknown physical state without inventing success or blindly redispatching.
candidateMechanism: narrow structured effects only where full effect contract exists (self-release, Workspace Patch)
units.counterfactualDeletion: Remove Runtime while keeping Host, Harness, Git and systemd: Tasks can still exist and Agents can still choose actions, but applications again hand-roll request identity, Workspace/source binding, process-tree ownership, retained output association, cancellation races and response-loss recovery. Lost responses easily become duplicate physical dispatch or guessed completion.
units.semanticChoice: Caller/Agent chooses the admitted action; caller/domain decides whether its result is useful/correct.
units.durableStructuralState: Runtime Registry and digest-bound execution evidence own Job/Attempt physical continuity.
units.physicalTruth: Git + Runtime Registry + systemd/cgroup + digest-bound Runner/Artifact files under the Runtime contract.
units.externalEffectTruth: Not generic Runtime truth. Arbitrary workspace.exec is OPAQUE; an external provider/domain or narrow structured effect adapter must supply identity/receipt/reconciliation semantics for the external effect itself.
proofBoundaries: One Attempt crosses physical dispatch at most once; this is not exactly-once external effect.
Execution Result != External Effect Receipt != Semantic Completion.
Ambiguous dispatch is preserved, not speculatively repeated.
trusted_local is owner-trusted execution, not hostile multi-tenant isolation.
contained_local reduces ambient authority but is not kernel-grade hostile isolation.
Host Dependency path witnessing is not proof of target-byte consumption or complete environment closure.

units.disposition: retain; physical truth boundary is strongly justified, generic external-effect ownership remains rejected
units.expectedCapability: An Agent can turn an admitted local action into an exact durable physical operation, recover after interruption without duplicating ambiguous work, and receive truthful execution evidence while leaving external-effect and semantic truth to their actual owners.
commonMisconceptions: process exit 0 proves the Agent objective is complete.
a shell command can be declared idempotent/read-only by the caller.
Runtime should model all external effects.
units.feynman: Runtime is the part that can answer 'what exact local action did we really start, what process tree belonged to it, what bytes came back, and what do we still not know after a crash?' It makes physical execution recoverable; it does not turn a successful process into proof that the outside world changed correctly or that the user's goal was achieved.

retain: causal reconstruction as an internal existence audit
multi-axis ownership rather than one primary owner
reject: pure causal prose as automatically superior Agent-facing representation
single primary-owner classification as a general explanation ontology
forcing classical delegation, local ownership and no-new-shared-layer into mutually exclusive categories
methodDisposition.deferToStudioWeb: Whether causal narrative, diagrams, stories or repository-first tables better teach humans is an expression/comprehension question still to be experimentally tested; EX1 only tested fresh model Agents.
